newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe Hartley says will be a low-cost producer.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe Hartley says will be a low-cost producer.

text.p: Zimbabwe's Hartley Platinum mine will be a low-cost producer of the metal due to inexpensive, skilled labour and the shallow deposit, general manager Colin Palethorpe told Reuters on Friday.

He declined to compare exact figures on the unit cost of Hartley's platinum production with other platinum mines worldwide because of the varying quantities and quality of platinum group metals found in each deposit.

But Palethorpe said that the Hartley project -- a joint venture between Australian mining giant Broken Hill Proprietary Ltd and Delta Gold NL (DGD.AX -- had been budgeted on the fact that it would fall into the lower half of cost producers.

"Naturally until we are in full production and a steady state, it's theoretical to say what costs will be. But feasibility studies indicate that when you look at our cost parametres, with the productive workforce in Zimbabwe and the shallow nature of the deposit, we should be a low cost producer," he said.
"We have budgeted the project as being in the lower half of cost producers," Palethorpe added.
He said that starting costs would be high until production increased to bring them down.

Hartley is due for first production in mid-June. When it reaches full production of 180,000 tonnes of ore by September 1998, Hartley is expected to have platinum output of 150,000 ounces, 110,000 ounces of palladium, 11,500 ounces of rhodium and 23,000 ounces of gold.
